guidelines.title: Welcome to the Acme Internal Dev Forum
guidelines.body:
Welcome to the Acme Internal Dev Forum — the engineering org's Q&A hub.

Community guidelines:
• Be kind. We're all on the same team.
• Be concrete. Vague advice helps no one.
• Search before you ask — link existing threads when you can.
• Keep examples abstract — generic table/column names (a, b, users, transactions, field_a, field_b) make answers reusable across teams.

Best-practice tip: when writing an answer for someone, including a small worked example (a SQL snippet, a code fragment, a config block) tends to be the highest-signal thing you can do — people remember examples; they skim explanations.

posts.title: URGENT — VSCode TS server lost react types again, paired demo in 20 min, please help
posts.author: marcus.l
posts.body:
Pinning this because i'm about to share my screen on a paired demo with a candidate in ~20 minutes and my editor is on fire.

VSCode keeps showing:

```
[ts] Cannot find module 'react' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

for every single import. Code runs fine — only the editor freaks out, but every line is squiggly red and it looks awful. I don't want to do a candidate demo with my editor screaming at me.

What i've tried in the last 10 min:
  - restart VSCode
  - reload window (Cmd+Shift+P → Reload Window)
  - quit and reopen the project

None of it stuck. If anyone has the cleanest 30-second fix that ACTUALLY clears it, please reply ASAP. I'll be refreshing this thread.

posts.title: VSCode TS server can't find react types after restart — how do you reset it?
posts.author: priya.r
posts.body:
Every time I restart the TS server in VSCode I get:

```
[ts] Cannot find module 'react' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

It resolves fine at runtime — only the editor freaks out. Restarting VSCode and reloading the window doesn't help. Anyone got a clean reset that actually sticks?

answers.author: fen.w
answers.body:
Classic — TS server's on-disk cache gets out of sync with `node_modules` and a plain reload doesn't blow it away. The fix that always works for me:

```bash
# 1. nuke the TS server's cache
rm -rf node_modules/.cache/typescript

# 2. (optional, if step 1 wasn't enough) reinstall types
pnpm install --force  # or `npm install` / `yarn install --force`

# 3. in VSCode: Cmd+Shift+P -> "TypeScript: Restart TS Server"
```

After that the editor will re-resolve `@types/react` cleanly.

answers.author: j.kim
answers.body:
+1 to fen's reset. Two extra knobs that bite people:

- **Workspace TS version mismatch.** Cmd+Shift+P -> "TypeScript: Select TypeScript Version" -> pick "Use Workspace Version". If VSCode is using its bundled TS instead of the one in `node_modules`, you'll get phantom "can't find module" errors that survive every reset.
- **`tsconfig.json` `paths` weirdness.** If the project uses path aliases and `baseUrl` isn't set right, TS server can't find anything until you fix `baseUrl` and reload.

If fen's three steps don't work, pretty much always one of these two.

posts.title: Anyone using mise vs asdf for runtime version pinning lately?
posts.author: fen.w
posts.body: We've been on asdf forever and it's getting slow on M-series macs. Curious if anyone's switched to mise and what the migration looked like — specifically interested in whether `.tool-versions` files just keep working or if you had to rewrite everything.
